title: The Book of Haggai Timeline
sub: Consider Your Ways · Rebuild the Temple
desc: Returned exiles who built paneled houses for themselves while the temple sat in ruins are confronted, respond immediately, and are promised the new temple's latter splendor will exceed even Solomon's.

eras.label: Era One · Haggai 1
eras.name: Consider Your Ways — Rebuild the Temple
eras.dates: Sixteen years after returning from exile, the people have built paneled houses for themselves while the LORD's temple sits in ruins

events.title: Is It Right for You to Live in Paneled Houses While My Temple Is in Ruins?
events.detail: Haggai confronts the returned exiles for prioritizing their own comfortable homes over rebuilding the temple, diagnosing their economic frustration — planting much but harvesting little — as a direct consequence of that misplaced priority.

verses.text: “Is it right for you to live in richly paneled houses while my temple is in ruins?”

events.title: The People Obeyed the LORD — Work on the Temple Begins
events.detail: Remarkably, the leaders and people respond immediately to the rebuke, obeying the LORD and beginning work on the temple within three weeks of the prophet's first message.

verses.text: “Go up to the hill country and bring back timber to build the temple. Then I will be pleased and honored,” says the LORD [Yahweh].

eras.label: Era Two · Haggai 2
eras.name: The Latter Glory of This House — a Signet Ring
eras.dates: Three more oracles in one month encourage a discouraged rebuilding crew, promise a coming shaking of the nations, and single out Zerubbabel for a personal blessing

events.title: Take Heart — the Latter Splendor of This House Will Be Greater
events.detail: To builders discouraged that the new temple looks unimpressive next to Solomon's, the LORD of Heaven's Armies promises he is with them and that this temple's future splendor will exceed the former, with peace given in that place.

verses.text: “Be strong, O Zerubbabel,” declares the LORD [Yahweh]… “and work, for I am with you,” declares the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies.
“The future splendor of this temple will be greater than that of former times,” the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies has declared. “And in this place I will give peace.”

events.title: A Ritual Question — From Today I Will Bless You
events.detail: Using a priestly ruling about ritual purity, Haggai illustrates how the people's former disobedience contaminated all their efforts, then pivots to a fresh promise: from this day of renewed obedience forward, blessing will follow.

verses.text: “The seed is still in the storehouse, isn't it? And the vine, fig tree, pomegranate, and olive tree have not produced. Nevertheless, from today on I will bless you.”

events.title: I Will Make You Like a Signet Ring — Zerubbabel Chosen
events.detail: On the same day, a final oracle promises a future overthrow of earthly kingdoms and singles out Zerubbabel, of the Davidic line, as the LORD's chosen signet ring — a term reversing the curse once pronounced on his ancestor Jeconiah.

verses.text: “‘On that day,’ says the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies, ‘I will take you, Zerubbabel… and I will make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you.’”
